newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Tuesday were steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, buoyed by relatively light hog movement and strong packer demand, livewtock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $56.50 to $57.50 at plants, sources there said.
Illinois hogs sold $0.50 higher at $56.00 to $56.50 in the country and $57.00 to $57.50 at plants.
"Some packers are short and chasing pretty hard for hogs," a Illinois dealer said.

Indiana hogs sold $0.50 higher at $56.50 to $57.00 in the country and $57.50 to $58.00 at plants. Some packers reportedly were paying up to $60.00 for top quality hogs because of the tight supplies, dealers said.
Ohio hogs sold steady, but with a firm tone, at $54.00 to $55.00 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants.

Strong packer demand also was fueled by higher pork prices, which eased poor operating margins, although several packer buyers still reported negative margins. Pork prices were bolstered by firm retail demand for summer cookout and pre-Independence Day holiday promotions, sources said.
